chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Musa, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Marwak ibn Ubayd, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) forbade a man from hunting fish on Friday before the prayer, and he (peace be upon him) would pass by the fishmongers on Friday and forbid them from hunting fish on Friday before the prayer.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib)
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: the prayer (specifically congregational Friday prayer in this context)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on fishing or hunting fish on Friday before the congregational prayer in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the practical application of Friday's sanctity by Imam Ali (AS), extending the prohibition of hunting to fishing to prevent distraction from congregational prayers. It underscores the scholarly view that commercial activities, such as those of fishmongers, should be suspended or minimized during the sacred time of Jumu'ah to maintain spiritual focus and community cohesion.
